nodes.name: Low-temperature pyrolysis with Se
nodes.procedure: The hollow Ni/FeMn@CoNiSe nanocages could be prepared in one step by mixing PBA-P with Se powder followed by pyrolysis at 350°C in an Ar atmosphere. For clarity, this material was named as PBA-Se 350. Here, as the core PBAs obtained in the first stage of the synthesis are expected to contain more defect sites, they are more susceptible to dissolution during the pyrolysis step. Therefore, this enables their selective dissolution to yield a hollow interior under our proposed conditions.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals cubic shape with uniform edge length of 121±22 nm for PBA-Se 350 nanocages.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) image (Figure 1a; Figure S1, Supporting Information) reveals the samples' cubic shape and relatively uniform edge length (121±22 nm).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows formation of hollow interior within cubic nanocages and uniform distribution of small NP islands (sizes below 15 nm) decorating the surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images (Figure 1b,c) show the formation of a hollow interior within the cubic nanocages.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern shows two sets of electron diffraction patterns assigned to PBAs and metallic Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To confirm this, the selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern and high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images were obtained. As displayed in Figure 1c, the two sets of electron diffraction patterns can be assigned to PBAs and metallic Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals characteristic crystalline lattice spacings of FeMn and CoNi PBAs, and lattice fringes with interplanar spacings of 0.205 nm corresponding to the (111) diffraction planes of metallic Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM analyses of the FeMn core and CoNi shell regions... reveal characteristic crystalline lattice spacings of FeMn and CoNi PBAs (Figure 1e). The HRTEM images in Figure 1e together with high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) images also reveal lattice fringes with interplanar spacings of 0.205 nm, corresponding to the (111) diffraction planes of metallic Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM images show surface features and confirm lattice fringes of metallic Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM images in Figure 1e together with high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) images also reveal lattice fringes with interplanar spacings of 0.205 nm...

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM-EDS elemental mapping shows incorporation and uniform distribution of Se, Fe, Co, Mn, Ni in PBA-Se 350 nanocages.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The STEM-EDS elemental mapping (Figure 1g) shows the incorporation and uniform distribution of Se into PBA-Se 350 nanocages during the synthesis.

nodes.characterization_summary: Powder XRD supports electron microscopy results for PBA-derived materials.
nodes.evidence_snippet: All the PBA-derived materials (PBA-Se 350 and control samples PBA-300 and PBA-350) were also interrogated by powder X-ray diffraction (XRD), Raman, UV-vis, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and electron spin resonance (ESR) (Figure S7, Supporting Information), supporting the results from the electron microscopy analysis.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectroscopy supports electron microscopy results.
nodes.evidence_snippet: All the PBA-derived materials... were also interrogated by powder X-ray diffraction (XRD), Raman, UV-vis, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and electron spin resonance (ESR) (Figure S7, Supporting Information), supporting the results from the electron microscopy analysis.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS supports electron microscopy results; post-OER XPS shows oxidation state changes including disappearance of Ni⁰ peak and formation of higher valence metal species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: All the PBA-derived materials... were also interrogated by powder X-ray diffraction (XRD), Raman, UV-vis, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS)... The XPS spectra of the catalyst (Figure 3e) also display significant differences before and after the OER testing.

nodes.characterization_summary: ESR shows decreased signal for PBA-Se 350 compared to PBA-Ar 350, demonstrating Se doping suppresses CN vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The effect of Se doping on the suppression of CN vacancies in Prussian blue analogs was examined by comparing the ESR spectra of PBA-Se 350 and PBA 350 samples (Figure S7i, Supporting Information). The results showed a decrease in the ESR signal of PBA-Se 350 compared to that of PBA-Ar 350...

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows transformation from Ni(OH)₂ (445, 521 cm⁻¹) at 1.1 V to NiOOH (485, 559 cm⁻¹) at 1.3 V, with further changes at 1.5 V due to MnOOH formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To investigate the dynamic rearrangement behavior of the PBA-Se 350 catalyst during the OER process, the in situ Raman spectra were acquired... At the beginning of the electrocatalytic process (1.1 V) two characteristic Raman signals centered ≈445 and 521 cm⁻¹ were observed... As the voltage was increased to 1.3 V, these signals disappeared, and two new peaks were detected at 485 and 559 cm⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface area results consistent with C_dl measurements, indicating hollow structure provides more exposed active sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: PBA-Se 350 exhibits a C_dl value of 6.09 mF cm⁻²... which were also consistent with the Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area results (Figure S10, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS illustrates changes in relative atomic ratio after OER test.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDS and inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry results also illustrate the changes in the relative atomic ratio after the OER test (Table S3, Supporting Information).
